objective: Let a local product owner attach one immutable operator-supplied review delivery to an approved Implementation Brief and let Elder consume the product-owned Git delivery contract without bypassing authority.
scope: Add the Review Deliveries bounded context and brief-to-delivery workflow.
Create at most one immutable delivery for an existing Implementation Brief in a locked PostgreSQL transaction.
Persist the exact repository, base and head branches, commit SHA, pull-request number and URL, verification summary, unverified local submitter label, and server time.
Add POST /api/v1/implementation-briefs/{implementationBriefId}/review-delivery and an additive reviewDelivery Signal-detail projection.
Expose the implementation-to-review trace through the local product interface without claiming hosted-provider verification.
Add and validate a product-owned machine-readable Git delivery contract with ordered checks and retained authority.
Attempt Elder consumption and hosted delivery under current authority, correct only a reproduced consumption blocker, record actor attribution, close the learning loop, and stop.
non_goals: Delivery editing, deletion, multiple attempts, status workflow, release notes, or customer communication.
GitHub API verification, credentials, commit signing, PR creation from the product, merge, deployment, or release.
Authentication, authorization, verified identity, tenancy, public hosting, production, L2 or L3 promotion, or constitutional changes.
SD-005, merge of Elder PR #3 or #4, or a change to the canonical observation threshold.
evidence_plan: Foundation: validate ADR, contract, work item, delivery policy, Prisma schema, migration, source layout, boundaries, types, lint, and route surface.
Component: prove deterministic delivery-policy validation, branch, commit, URL, acknowledgement, bounds, content checks, and server identity/time binding.
Integration: prove source brief locking, one immutable delivery per brief, exact lineage, concurrency rejection, policy-derived repository, and PostgreSQL constraints.
Workflow: create the complete feedback-to-review-delivery trace through the local UI and observe persistence after reload at desktop and mobile widths.
Stress: prove concurrent delivery creation has one winner, malformed and missing sources fail closed, database outage recovers with lineage intact, and delivery content is absent from logs.
Factory: validate contract consumption, record P5.2 readiness truth and actor attribution, deliver only under explicit owner authority, and propose candidate learning without promotion.
